title: Ashirwad Scheme Punjab 2026: ₹51,000 Marriage Grant
meta_description: Punjab Ashirwad Scheme 2026: ₹51,000 one-time grant for SC/BC/EWS girls' marriage. Apply at ashirwad.punjab.gov.in. Eligibility, documents, portal guide.

hero.one_liner: Punjab Ashirwad Scheme gives Rs 51,000 as a one-time marriage grant to SC, BC and EWS daughters. Eligibility, the 30-day window, documents, and how to apply.

what_is_it: The Ashirwad Scheme is a Punjab government programme that provides ₹51,000 as a one-time marriage grant to families from economically weaker sections at the time of their daughter's wedding. It was previously known as the Shagun Scheme before being renamed and expanded under the current administration.
The ₹51,000 amount is the same across all eligible categories. There is no distinction between SC, BC, OBC, or EWS families.

eligibility.value: Not more than Rs 32,790 per year from all sources.

eligibility_filters.notes: Bride 18+, Punjab resident, family income under Rs 32,790/yr, SC/BC/EWS or widow's daughter. Up to 2 daughters per family. Apply within 30 days before or after marriage.

how_to_apply.title: Open ashirwad.punjab.gov.in
how_to_apply.description: Go to the official Ashirwad portal at ashirwad.punjab.gov.in. This is the only official application portal for the scheme. Do not use any third-party site that claims to help with Ashirwad applications, they cannot submit on your behalf and may misuse your documents.

how_to_apply.title: Register on the portal
how_to_apply.description: Click the Registration link on the homepage. Fill in the basic details, family name, mobile number, Aadhaar number, district, and category (SC/BC/EWS/Widow's daughter). Submit to create your account. You will receive a Registered ID and a password via SMS on the registered mobile number.

how_to_apply.title: Log in and open the application form
how_to_apply.description: Use your Registered ID and password to log in. Navigate to the Ashirwad Scheme application section. Open the online application form. Fill in all required fields: bride's details, marriage date, family income, bank account number and IFSC code. Double-check the bank account number and IFSC, even a single digit error means the payment goes to a wrong account, and recovering a failed DBT transfer takes weeks.

how_to_apply.title: Upload all required documents
how_to_apply.description: Upload the scanned copies of all required documents: Aadhaar, caste/income certificate, age proof, bank passbook, and marriage certificate (if post-wedding). Ensure each file is legible and within the file size limit shown on the portal.

how_to_apply.title: Submit and note the application number
how_to_apply.description: Submit the completed form. The portal will generate an Application Number or reference ID. Note this number immediately, it is the only identifier for tracking your application status. You will also receive a confirmation SMS.

how_to_apply.title: Track your application status
how_to_apply.description: Log back into ashirwad.punjab.gov.in using your ID and password to check the status of your application. The status updates through stages: submitted, under verification, approved, payment initiated, and paid. If status is stuck at 'under verification' for more than 3-4 weeks, visit your District Social Welfare Office under the Department of Social Justice, Empowerment and Minorities in your district. Carry a printout of the application summary page showing your application number, and be prepared to show original documents if the officer asks to verify your submission.

ministry: Department of Social Justice, Empowerment and Minorities, Punjab

extra_sections.heading: What Is the Ashirwad Scheme
content: The scheme is administered by the Department of Social Justice, Empowerment and Minorities, Government of Punjab. Applications are made through the dedicated portal ashirwad.punjab.gov.in, and the grant is transferred directly to the beneficiary's bank account via DBT, no middlemen, no cash handling.
The scheme covers daughters of widows regardless of caste. A widow from a general category family whose income is below ₹32,790/year can apply for Ashirwad for her daughter's marriage.
This is a meaningful inclusion because widow-headed households are often excluded from caste-based welfare schemes.

The scheme also applies to Muslim girls aged 18 or above, alongside SC, Christian, BC, and EWS families and daughters of widows of any caste. The grant is the same Rs 51,000 for every eligible community.
An offline route exists through the District Welfare Office for families without internet access. The form can be downloaded, filled, and submitted in person with documents.
The Chief Minister clarified that the grant applies to Muslim girls of 18 or above as well. This keeps the scheme open across communities within the income limit.

extra_sections.heading: Who the Grant Covers
content: The grant also covers SC and Christian widows or divorcees at the time of their own remarriage, not just the marriage of their daughters. This is an often-overlooked provision.
If an SC or Christian woman who is widowed or divorced is getting married again, she can apply personally as the beneficiary.
The scheme is limited to two daughters per family over its lifetime. A family that has already received the Ashirwad grant for one daughter can apply again for a second daughter.
A third application from the same family will be rejected regardless of eligibility.
Districts sometimes ask for a Sarpanch or ward councillor letter confirming income. This is supplementary and does not replace the Tehsildar or SDM income certificate.
Families who received the grant for an older daughter can apply again for a second daughter. The two-daughter limit applies across the family's lifetime, not per year.

extra_sections.heading: Income Limit and Category Rules
content: The income limit of ₹32,790 per year is low by most urban standards but reflects the scheme's focus on very poor families. In practical terms, ₹32,790 per year is about ₹2,667 per month in total household income from all sources including agricultural income, daily wage labour, small business, and any other earning.
Families who are above this limit, say a household where the father earns ₹4,000 a month as an unskilled labourer, do not qualify, even if they are SC or BC.

The scheme is part of a broader set of marriage-assistance programmes across Indian states. Punjab's Ashirwad grant at ₹51,000 is among the higher amounts in this category, comparable to West Bengal's Rupashree Prakalpa (₹25,000), UP's Kanya Vivah Yojana, and similar programmes.
The higher amount reflects Punjab's higher cost of living relative to some other states.
If a payment is credited to a wrong account due to an entry error, contact the District Social Welfare Office quickly. Correcting bank details early prevents a long recovery process.
The Ashirwad Shagun component and the main Ashirwad grant are part of the same scheme. Shagun is simply the older Punjabi name for the marriage gift.

extra_sections.heading: How the Grant Amount Grew Over Time
content: The scheme began in 1997 as the Shagun Scheme with a much smaller grant. It was renamed Ashirwad and the amount was raised in stages, from Rs 15,000 to Rs 21,000, and then to Rs 51,000 from 1 July 2021.
The Rs 51,000 figure is the current grant and applies equally to every eligible category. There is no separate higher or lower amount for SC, BC, or EWS families.
Once approved, the money usually reaches the bride's account within 15 to 30 days through DBT. No cash is handled at any stage.
Some districts additionally ask for a ration card copy as supplementary income proof. This is not universal, so check what your district welfare office requires.

extra_sections.title: The 30-Day Window: Do Not Miss It
extra_sections.content:
Apply up to 30 days before the marriage or within 30 days after it. Applications more than 30 days after the wedding are rejected.

Most families apply after the wedding. If you do, submit within 30 days and do not wait to collect documents slowly, or you lose the Rs 51,000.

extra_sections.heading: How Much and How It Is Paid
content: The ₹51,000 amount is the same across all eligible categories. There is no distinction in the grant amount between SC, BC/OBC, or EWS families, all qualifying families receive ₹51,000.
The Ashirwad Shagun component (marriage gift) and the main Ashirwad grant are part of the same scheme.

The income certificate required for the scheme must be obtained from the Tehsildar or SDM (Sub-Divisional Magistrate). This certificate is free of cost from the government office but may require a few visits and some waiting time.
Get it well in advance of the marriage, ideally 2-3 months before the wedding date, so you are within the application window from the beginning.

extra_sections.title: One-Time Marriage Grant by DBT
extra_sections.desc:
The grant is the same Rs 51,000 across all eligible categories, paid by DBT to the bride's bank account.

It was raised from Rs 21,000 to Rs 51,000 in 2021. A family can claim it for up to two daughters over the scheme's lifetime.

extra_sections.heading: Documents You Must Submit
content: The core documents needed are: Aadhaar card of the bride, residence proof confirming permanent Punjab residency (Aadhaar or voter ID works), income certificate from a competent authority (Tehsildar or SDM) showing annual family income does not exceed ₹32,790, and bank account details (passbook copy) of the bride.
For SC applicants: a caste certificate issued by a competent authority confirming Scheduled Caste status. For BC/OBC applicants: an OBC or Backward Class certificate.
For EWS applicants: an Economically Weaker Section certificate. For daughters of widows: the widow's Aadhaar and a death certificate of the deceased husband.
Punjab released around Rs 301 crore in 2024-25, helping over 38,000 SC families and about 20,000 BC families. Further releases continued through 2025-26.

items.title: Bride's Aadhaar
items.sub: Must show a Punjab address. If it shows another state's address, update it before applying or the application is rejected.

items.title: Income certificate
items.sub: From a Tehsildar or SDM, confirming family income is under Rs 32,790 a year. This is the document most often rejected when wrong.

items.title: Caste certificate
items.sub: SC certificate for SC applicants, OBC/BC certificate for BC applicants, from a competent authority.

items.title: Age and marriage proof
items.sub: Aadhaar or Class 10 certificate for age 18+, plus a marriage registration or religious-institution certificate if applying after the wedding.

items.title: Bride's bank account
items.sub: In the bride's own name, Aadhaar-linked for DBT. Open one before applying if she does not have one.

extra_sections.heading: Caste, Age and Marriage Proof
content: Age proof for the bride confirming she is 18 years or above on the marriage date. Acceptable documents include Aadhaar card, Class 10 board certificate, birth certificate, or any government-issued document with date of birth.

Marriage-related documents: if applying after the marriage, a marriage registration certificate or certificate from the religious institution where the marriage was performed. If applying before the marriage, the marriage invitation card or a declaration of the proposed marriage date from the local Sarpanch or Ward Member may be accepted.
Beneficiaries span districts from Barnala and Bathinda to Ludhiana, Jalandhar, and Malerkotla. The spread shows the scheme reaches poor families across rural and urban Punjab.

extra_sections.title: Ashirwad and Shagun Are the Same Scheme
extra_sections.content:
Shagun is the older name. The scheme was renamed Ashirwad and the grant raised over the years.

If you see Ashirwad Shagun, Shagun Yojana, or Ashirwad Scheme, they all refer to this one programme on the same ashirwad.punjab.gov.in portal.

extra_sections.heading: Applying on the Ashirwad Portal
content: One common point of confusion: the 'Ashirwad Shagun' and 'Ashirwad Scheme' are not two different schemes. Shagun is a Punjabi/Hindi word for an auspicious gift given at the time of marriage, and the full scheme is commonly referred to by both names.
All applications go through the same portal and the same process.

The Ashirwad portal also serves as the application window for certain other welfare schemes run by the Punjab Social Justice Department. When you register and log in, you may see options for other schemes alongside Ashirwad.
Each scheme has its own eligibility and application form, the Ashirwad application is specifically for the marriage grant, not for all schemes visible on the portal.

extra_sections.title: Use Only the Official Portal
extra_sections.content:
The only official application portal is ashirwad.punjab.gov.in. Do not use any third-party site that claims to file for you.

The portal handles registration, submission, upload, and status tracking. Payment moves through PFMS/DBT after district approval, usually 3 to 7 working days.

extra_sections.heading: After You Apply: Payment Timeline
content: The Punjab government periodically releases funds to districts for disbursement under the Ashirwad scheme. When a district's allocation for a quarter is disbursed and the next allocation has not yet arrived, approved applications may be in a brief holding state before payment is initiated.
This is district-level cash flow management, not a rejection. If your application is approved but payment is delayed beyond 2-3 weeks, a brief wait is normal before escalation is needed.

For families that applied for and received the Ashirwad grant for an older daughter and are now applying for a second daughter, the process is the same. Log in with your existing Registered ID and submit a fresh application for the second marriage.
The portal tracks the family's history, so it will automatically flag if a third application is attempted from the same family.

items.title: Wrong income certificate
items.sub: The top rejection reason. Get it from a Tehsildar or SDM, not a panchayat member or ward councillor.

items.title: Name mismatch
items.sub: Aadhaar and bank account names must match. A married woman who changed her name should update the bank record first.

items.title: Stuck verification
items.sub: If status stays under verification beyond four weeks, visit the District Social Welfare Office with your reference number.

items.title: Reapplying after rejection
items.sub: Check the rejection reason on the portal, fix that specific issue, and resubmit rather than filing fresh.

extra_sections.heading: Why Applications Get Rejected
content: Application rejected for income certificate: the most common rejection reason is an income certificate issued by a non-competent authority. Punjab requires the income certificate to be issued by the Tehsildar, SDM, or an officer of the Revenue Department.
A certificate from a Sarpanch, Ward Member, or private notary is not accepted. Get a fresh certificate from the Revenue Department before reapplying.

Application stuck at 'under verification' for more than 4 weeks: this usually means the district welfare office has a backlog or there is a document query. Visit your District Social Welfare Office (under the Department of Social Justice, Empowerment and Minorities) with your application number and printed copies of all uploaded documents.
Ask specifically about the status and whether any document is incomplete.

extra_sections.text: The ashirwad.punjab.gov.in portal handles registration, application submission, document upload, and status tracking. It does not initiate the payment, that goes through PFMS/DBT after district-level approval. If your status shows 'approved' but the money has not arrived, the payment is in the banking system and typically takes 3-7 working days after approval to appear in your account.

extra_sections.heading: Scale of Disbursement in Punjab
content: In 2024-25 Punjab released around Rs 301 crore under the scheme, helping tens of thousands of SC and BC families with marriage costs. Further releases continued through 2025-26 across most districts.
Beneficiaries come from districts across the state, from Bathinda and Sangrur to Ludhiana, Jalandhar, and Malerkotla. This wide spread shows the scheme reaches both rural and urban poor families.
An offline route exists through the District Welfare Office for families without internet access. The form can be downloaded, filled, and submitted with documents in person.

faqs.question: What is the punjab ashirwad scheme and how much does it pay?
faqs.answer:
The Punjab Ashirwad Scheme (formerly Shagun Scheme) provides ₹51,000 as a one-time marriage grant to families from SC, BC/OBC, EWS sections, and daughters of widows at the time of a girl's marriage. The amount is transferred via DBT to the bride's bank account.

The scheme is applied for through ashirwad.punjab.gov.in.

faqs.question: What is the ashirwad scheme eligibility?
faqs.answer:
The bride must be 18 years or above. Family annual income must not exceed ₹32,790 from all sources.

The family must belong to SC, BC/OBC, or EWS category, OR be a widow's family (any caste), OR the applicant must be an SC/Christian widow or divorcee applying for her own remarriage. Permanent Punjab residency is required.

Maximum 2 daughters per family.

faqs.question: How to apply on the ashirwad portal punjab?
faqs.answer:
Go to ashirwad.punjab.gov.in and click Registration. Fill in your details to create an account and receive a Registered ID and password.

Log in, open the Ashirwad application form, fill in the bride's and family's details, upload required documents (Aadhaar, income certificate, caste certificate, age proof, bank passbook), and submit. Note your Application Number for status tracking.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for the ashirwad scheme?
faqs.answer: Bride's Aadhaar card, residence proof, income certificate from Tehsildar/SDM (showing income ≤₹32,790/year), caste or category certificate (SC/BC/EWS), bride's age proof, bank account passbook of the bride (Aadhaar-linked), and marriage certificate or proof of marriage date. For daughters of widows, add the widow mother's Aadhaar and husband's death certificate.

faqs.question: What is the last date to apply for ashirwad scheme after marriage?
faqs.answer:
Applications must be submitted within 30 days of the marriage date. Applications filed more than 30 days after the wedding are rejected.

You can also apply up to 30 days before the marriage. Do not delay, collect and upload all documents within the first two weeks after the wedding to stay well within the 30-day window.

faqs.question: Can a widow's daughter from a general caste apply for ashirwad scheme?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Daughters of widows are eligible regardless of their caste.

Even if the family belongs to the general category (not SC, BC, or EWS), if the mother is a widow and the family income is below ₹32,790/year and the bride is 18 or above, the application qualifies. The widow must be the parent/guardian of the bride.

faqs.question: Is the ashirwad shagun scheme the same as ashirwad scheme?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Ashirwad Shagun refers to the same scheme, 'Shagun' is a Punjabi/Hindi word for an auspicious gift given at marriage, and the scheme was previously called the Shagun Scheme before being renamed Ashirwad Scheme.

Both names refer to the same ₹51,000 marriage grant programme with the same portal and eligibility.

faqs.question: My ashirwad application shows approved but money hasn't come. What do I do?
faqs.answer:
An approved status means the district has cleared the grant but payment is in the DBT pipeline. Check your bank account for a credit from a government/PFMS source, it typically arrives within 3-7 working days of approval.

If it has been more than 10 working days after approval with no credit, check your Aadhaar-bank seeding status at myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/bank-seeding-status and contact your District Social Welfare Office.
